extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulewriters and managers, OMB/OIRA/GSA staff, policy analysts, and members of the public interested in federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting entries for the semiannual Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions, including what actions to report, what agencies are covered, and statutory/Executive Order reporting obligations. Applies to agency staff who compile regulatory agendas for Reginfo.gov and the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of agencies included
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unified Agenda covers approximately 60 departments, agencies, and commissions across the Federal Government; agencies of the United States Congress are not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies across the executive branch (Cabinet, Executive, and Independent agencies) should submit agendas. Congressional entities are excluded from the Agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary inclusion criterion for actions (12‑month horizon)
rubrics_metrics.description: The activities included in individual agency agendas are primarily those currently planned to have an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM), a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), or a Final Rule issued within the next 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report items that are expected to move to an ANPRM, NPRM, or Final Rule within 12 months of publication of the Agenda so users can identify near-term opportunities for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long‑Term Actions listing
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may list in the 'Long‑Term Actions' section those rules it expects will have the next regulatory action more than 12 months after publication of the agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long‑Term Actions are used to keep the public informed of future rulemakings. When an agency subsequently schedules a regulatory action on one of these rules within a 12‑month timeframe, the item will reappear in the appropriate (near‑term) section of the agency's next agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completed Actions reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may report 'Completed Actions,' which are rulemakings that are being Withdrawn or ending their lifecycle with a regulatory action that completes the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Completed Actions to indicate rulemakings that have reached a terminal status (e.g., withdrawn or finalized) so the Agenda reflects lifecycle completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from agency agendas
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency agendas generally do not include regulations concerning military or foreign affairs functions and regulations related solely to agency organization, management, or personnel matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include purely internal organizational, personnel, or management rules or rules tied to military/foreign affairs functions in the Agenda; focus on substantive regulatory actions affecting the public or regulated parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fall edition requirement: The Regulatory Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Fall editions of the Unified Agenda include The Regulatory Plan, which presents agency statements of regulatory priorities and additional information about the most significant regulatory activities planned for the coming year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the fall submission, agencies should provide statements of regulatory priorities and expanded information on significant activities so they can be included in The Regulatory Plan portion of the Agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act reporting (small entity impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Flexibility Act (5 U.S.C. 601 et seq.) requires that agencies publish semiannual regulatory flexibility agendas in the Federal Register identifying those rules that may have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; agencies meet that requirement by including the information in their submissions for the Unified Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include in submissions any rules that may have significant economic impacts on many small entities and supply the information necessary to satisfy the RFA requirement; note that beginning with fall 2007 the Agenda published in the Federal Register has been limited in certain respects to regulatory flexibility agendas and The Regulatory Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and reporting of effects on state, local, and tribal governments; federalism implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 12866 and the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act direct agencies to assess the effects of Federal regulations on State, local, and tribal governments. Executive Order 13132 ('Federalism') directs agencies to have an accountable process to ensure meaningful and timely input by State and local officials in the development of regulatory policies that have 'federalism implications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should include in their submissions information on whether regulatory actions have effects on various levels of government, whether they have federalism implications (defined as actions that have substantial direct effects on the States, on the relationship between the National Government and the States, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities among levels of government), and whether they are subject to the Unfunded Mandates Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and audience of the Unified Agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Information Service Center compiles the Unified Agenda to provide information about Federal regulatory and deregulatory activities to the President and his Executive Office, the Congress, agency managers, and the public; Reginfo.gov is maintained as a public resource for information about Federal regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare Agenda entries with transparency and sufficient detail to inform senior officials, Congress, agency managers, and the public about regulatory priorities and planned actions; anticipate public use of Reginfo.gov for information and participation opportunities.
